what: Add Page Numbers to PDF stamps a number on every page of a PDF. You choose where the number goes, how it looks, which number to start from and how big it is.

It is useful for reports, theses, manuals, legal bundles and anything that will be printed or discussed in a meeting, where people need to say "look at page 12". It is also handy after merging several files, so the final document has one clear numbering.
The numbers are added inside your browser, and the PDF is not uploaded.
uses: Add clear page numbers before printing or submitting.
After joining files with Merge PDF, add one continuous numbering across all pages.
If this file is part 2 of a longer document, start at the number where part 1 ended.
Use "Page 1 of 10" so everyone knows how long the document is and can find pages fast.
Put numbers in a corner so they do not clash with headers or stamps.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop a PDF here" or drag a PDF onto the box. The tool shows the file name and page count.
Pick one of six places: "Bottom center", "Bottom right", "Bottom left", "Top center", "Top right" or "Top left". The number is placed about 1 cm (28 points) from the edge of the page.
"1" shows just the number. "1 / 10 (with the last number)" shows the number and the last number printed. "Page 1 of 10" writes it out in words. When you start at 1, the last number is the page count.

This is the number printed on the first page. It is 1 by default, and an empty box also means 1. Each next page counts up by one. Under the options, the tool shows the range it will use, for example "numbered 1 to 24". The last number is start + number of pages - 1.
"Small" is 9 point, "Medium" is 11 point and is the default, "Large" is 14 point. The numbers are dark gray in the Helvetica font.
A message such as "Numbered 24 pages from 1 to 24" appears. Click "Download PDF" to save the file, named like report-numbered.pdf.
features: Top or bottom, and left, center or right.
Start at 1, 0 or any other whole number.
Small, Medium or Large to match your document.
All pages get a number in one click, whatever their size.
The numbers are added on top. Your text stays selectable and images keep their quality.

example.title: Worked example: part 2 of a long report
example.text: Part 1 of Grace’s report ended on page 30, and part2.pdf has 20 pages. She sets "Start at" to 31, chooses "Bottom right" and the "Page 1 of 10" format. The last number is 31 + 20 - 1 = 50, so the first page shows "Page 31 of 50" and the last page shows "Page 50 of 50". She downloads part2-numbered.pdf.

tips: With "1 / 10" and "Page 1 of 10", the second number is the last page number, not the page count. If you start at 31 on a 20-page file, it shows "of 50". Use the plain "1" format if that would confuse readers.
Choose a corner position if the center of the footer already has text, such as a company name.
Merge all your files first, then add the numbers once, so numbering runs smoothly across the whole document.
Every page gets a number, including the cover. To leave the cover without one, split it off, number the rest starting at 2, then merge them back.
Running the tool twice on the same file adds a second set of numbers. Always start from the file without numbers.
problems: Your pages have very small margins. Try a different position, such as the top instead of the bottom, or a smaller text size.
The numbers appear sideways or on the wrong edge

The tool follows each page's built-in rotation, so numbers sit upright on the edge you chose as the page is shown. If a page still looks wrong, it may be a scan that was photographed sideways: fix it with Rotate PDF first.
The numbering starts at the wrong number
Check the "Start at" box. It sets the number on the first page of this file.
A message says "Start at" must be a whole number
Type a whole number from 0 to 999999, such as 1 or 31. Decimals and negative numbers are not allowed.
A message says the file "is password protected"
Remove the password in a PDF reader that knows it, save a copy, and use that copy.
